title: Sharpen org profile README opening to lead with logic-as-information-artifacts framing
description:
Rewrite the opening of the org profile README (`cmdrvl/.github/profile/README.md`, renders at github.com/cmdrvl) to lead with a sharper, more specific framing than the current "help agents answer hard data questions without hand-waving."

Target framing (validated in a 2026-09-03 LinkedIn exchange responding to a Vin post on AI/agents needing business logic as information models rather than embedded code): these tools externalize business logic — constraint sets (`verify`), registries (`canon`), schemas (`profile`), pattern definitions (`fingerprint`) — into declared, versioned, content-hashed artifacts instead of leaving it buried in application code or expecting an agent to infer it from a codebase it can't reliably query. The binaries themselves carry no embedded domain logic; 100% of the domain-specific behavior lives in the external artifact.

Keep the existing "What this feels like with an agent" before/after section and the two worked examples — those are good and concrete. Just sharpen the opening paragraph(s) so a first-time visitor immediately understands the tools are an implementation of "logic as information artifacts," not just "tools that reduce hand-waving."

Source: bd-3m5 audit, 2026-09-03.
close_reason: Rewrote README opening + restructured for simplicity, dropped spine wording per follow-up direction. Pushed 7b79055.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
Direction refinement from Zac (2026-09-03):

- Drop the word "spine" from all these surfaces (README, system prompt, install/tool copy) — it's internal jargon that adds no value externally. Applies to `SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`'s title/body ("Epistemic Spine System Prompt", "epistemic spine") and any other public-facing copy that uses it. Rename the file itself as part of the bd-3bd fix (folds into that work).
- De-slopify the text: cut AI-generated-sounding filler, keep it simple and direct.
- Shift the framing: don't try to make the human-facing README fully explain every mechanism. Keep the human-facing surface short and simple, and explicitly encourage handing the details off to the reader's own coding agent (paste the system prompt in, let the agent read `--describe`/`--schema`) for full understanding — the agent-facing docs carry the depth, not the README.

title: Audit and improve github.com/cmdrvl accessibility for agents and humans
description:
Audit and improve how github.com/cmdrvl and its agent-facing surfaces communicate the spine tools (vacuum, hash, fingerprint, profile, shape, rvl, verify, benchmark, assess, canon, lock, pack, veil, airlock, twinning, regret) — especially the framing that these tools work as business-logic-as-information-artifacts primitives for agents (constraint sets, registries, schemas, fingerprints — not embedded code logic), which is the angle that resonated in a recent LinkedIn exchange (Vin's "AI needs business logic as information models, not code" post, 2026-09-03).

Findings from initial audit (2026-09-03):

1. Org profile README (`cmdrvl/.github/profile/README.md`, renders at github.com/cmdrvl) is actually already fairly strong — has concrete examples, a "Start Here" table, quick start, and a "For Agent Builders" section. Opportunity: sharpen the opening framing to lead with "these tools externalize business logic into declared, versioned artifacts (constraint sets, registries, schemas) instead of leaving it embedded in code or expecting an agent to infer it" — this is a stronger, more specific hook than the current "help agents answer hard data questions without hand-waving" opener.

2. **Broken link, confirmed bug**: the README's "For Agent Builders" section links to `./SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`, but the actual file in the repo is named `SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` (`cmdrvl/.github/profile/SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`) — a rename that never got the README link updated. Confirmed 404 via `gh api repos/cmdrvl/.github/contents/profile/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`. `AGENT_PROMPT.md` (the other linked file) does exist and resolves fine.

3. The content of `SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` itself is solid — compact (~38 lines), copy-paste-ready, covers the pipeline, report tools, refusal handling, self-discovery (`--describe`/`--schema`). Minor gap: it doesn't mention `veil` or `airlock` in the install line or tool list, even though the org README's Shipped Tools table does.

4. **cmdrvl.com already has a GitHub link** — present in the footer (`data-cmdrvl-footer-link="primary"` → `https://github.com/cmdrvl`) and in the homepage's schema.org `sameAs` JSON-LD. So "ensure github link on cmdrvl.com" is mostly done; worth a quick check on whether it should also be more prominent than footer-only (e.g., surfaced from a dedicated open-source/tools page or the main nav), given the open-source CLI layer is a distinct audience from the consulting/data-product visitors the rest of the site targets.

5. **Gap: cmdrvl.com's agent-facing surfaces (llms.txt, llms-full.txt) never mention the open-source spine tools at all.** Confirmed via `curl https://cmdrvl.com/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` — both are entirely about the CMD+RVL consulting/data-product business (finance/procurement outcomes, evidence packs, MCP servers) with zero reference to github.com/cmdrvl, the spine tools, or a system-prompt link. An agent reading cmdrvl.com's own agent-facing index has no path to discover the open-source tools exist.

Scope for this epic: land the concrete fixes below, then re-review the whole surface end to end (org README opening framing, tool list completeness, cmdrvl.com llms.txt/llms-full.txt, and GitHub link prominence) against the accessibility bar Zac raised.

title: Design and ship open-source cmdrvl umbrella porcelain CLI for agent data workflows
description:
## Background & Rationale
The CMD+RVL spine ships 14 separate bare single-word binaries (`vacuum`, `hashbytes`, `fingerprint`, `profile`, `shape`, `rvl`, `canon`, `verify`, `assess`, `lock`, `pack`, `benchmark`, `veil`, `airlock`). While atomic Unix binaries are great for composable pipelines, this creates two real adoption bottlenecks for AI agents:

1. **Global PATH collision & discovery overhead:** Installing 14 generic single-word binaries risks OS/dev tool collisions (`hash` and `benchmark` already collided in Homebrew) and forces agents to inspect each binary individually.
2. **High multi-command ceremony:** Common end-to-end tasks require chaining 3-5 commands (`vacuum | hashbytes | fingerprint | lock`, `shape && rvl && pack seal`), which is why `cmdrvl/receipts` had to wrap them in bash scripts.

## Goal
Design and ship a thin, open-source `cmdrvl` umbrella porcelain CLI (following Pattern B from multi-tool family ergonomics: family-aware orchestrator binary) that dispatches to or embeds the atomic spine tools without replacing them.

## Core Surfaces
- `cmdrvl capabilities --json` — consolidated family catalog of installed spine versions, shared exit codes, envelope schema, and per-binary capabilities pointers.
- `cmdrvl doctor --json` / `cmdrvl --robot-triage` — single-call fleet health & version-drift check across all installed spine binaries.
- `cmdrvl inspect <file> [--sheet <name>] --json` — zero-retention single-file structural profiler (CSV/TSV/JSONL/Parquet/XLSX).
- `cmdrvl diff <old> <new> [--key K] --json` — runs `shape` gate then `rvl` explanation in one round-trip with structured stop handling.
- `cmdrvl receipt <old> <new> [--key K] --out <dir>` — native Rust equivalent of `receipts-csv` (`shape` -> `rvl` -> `pack seal` -> `pack verify`).
- `cmdrvl <subtool> ...` pass-through so teams can avoid polluting global PATH with 14 bare binaries if desired.

## Testing & Verification
- E2E tests covering `cmdrvl capabilities --json`, `cmdrvl doctor --json`, `cmdrvl diff`, `cmdrvl inspect`, and `cmdrvl receipt` against real fixtures.
- Determinism and non-TTY tests across all umbrella verbs.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture ADR and working open-source cmdrvl umbrella CLI shipping capabilities --json, doctor --json, inspect, diff, and receipt with E2E tests.

title: Fix broken Homebrew install commands and binary names across profile README and agent prompts
description:
## Background & Evidence
During a cross-repo agent-ergonomics review of `github.com/cmdrvl`, the copy-paste Homebrew install command in `profile/README.md`, `profile/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`, and `profile/AGENT_PROMPT.md` was found to fail on first try:

1. `profile/README.md` (lines 87-90) instructs `brew install cmdrvl/tap/{vacuum,hash,fingerprint,profile,lock,shape,rvl,verify,benchmark,assess,canon,pack,veil,airlock}` and claims `cmdrvl/tap/benchmark` installs as `cmdrvl-benchmark`.
2. `profile/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` (line 42) and `profile/AGENT_PROMPT.md` (line 290) also reference `cmdrvl/tap/hash`.
3. Actual formulae in `cmdrvl/homebrew-tap` are `cmdrvl-hash.rb` (installs binary `hashbytes`) and `cmdrvl-benchmark.rb` (installs binary `benchmark`, NOT `cmdrvl-benchmark`). Neither `hash.rb` nor `benchmark.rb` exists.

## Goal
Ensure the very first command an agent or human copies from the org profile works without error (Axiom 0: first-try inevitability).

## Deliverables
- Update `profile/README.md`, `profile/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`, and `profile/AGENT_PROMPT.md` to use the exact Homebrew formula names (`cmdrvl-hash`, `cmdrvl-benchmark`) and exact installed binary names (`hashbytes`, `benchmark`).
- Include `verify`, `assess`, and `cmdrvl-benchmark` cleanly in `SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` and `AGENT_PROMPT.md` install blocks (they are already published in `cmdrvl/homebrew-tap`).
- Add a lightweight CI check or script validating every `cmdrvl/tap/<formula>` referenced in `.github/profile/*.md` matches `cmdrvl/homebrew-tap/Formula/*.rb`.
acceptance_criteria: All brew install snippets in profile/README.md, profile/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md, and profile/AGENT_PROMPT.md reference existing cmdrvl/homebrew-tap formulae and accurate binary names (hashbytes, benchmark).

title: Update SYSTEM_PROMPT.md and AGENT_PROMPT.md for --explicit redaction, ~/.cmdrvl paths, and robot discovery surfaces
description:
## Background & Evidence
`profile/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` and `profile/AGENT_PROMPT.md` have drifted behind the actual shipped spine tools:

1. **Missing agent discovery surfaces:** Neither prompt mentions `--robot-triage`, `capabilities --json`, `robot-docs guide`, or `doctor`, even though ~12 spine tools now ship them. Agents pasted these prompts miss the primary one-call discovery surface.
2. **Stale witness path:** `AGENT_PROMPT.md` (line 102) still documents `~/.epistemic/witness.jsonl` instead of the canonical `~/.cmdrvl/state/witness/witness.jsonl`.
3. **Undocumented `--explicit` redaction default:** `shape` and `rvl` default to redacted output for zero-retention safety unless `--explicit` is passed, yet neither prompt mentions `--explicit` while showing unredacted output examples.
4. **Refusal/flag inaccuracies:** `AGENT_PROMPT.md` lists `E_INPUT_NOT_LOCKED` for `rvl` (which does not yet accept `--lock`), omits `s3-to-vacuum` (shipped in `vacuum.rb`), and notes `shape` `--profile` support as uncertain even though `shape` is profile-aware today.

## Goal
Bring `SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` and `AGENT_PROMPT.md` into 100% alignment with live spine contracts so agents get accurate instructions on the first read.

## Deliverables
- Document the read-only discovery workflow (`--robot-triage`, `capabilities --json`, `robot-docs guide`, `--describe`, `--schema`).
- Update witness and config footprint paths to `~/.cmdrvl/...` (noting `EPISTEMIC_WITNESS` override).
- Explicitly document `--explicit` zero-retention redaction behavior for `shape`/`rvl` (and when to pass it vs. stay redacted).
- Fix `rvl`/`shape` flag and refusal table inaccuracies and mention `s3-to-vacuum`.
acceptance_criteria: SYSTEM_PROMPT.md and AGENT_PROMPT.md accurately document --robot-triage/capabilities/robot-docs, ~/.cmdrvl paths, --explicit behavior, and live tool flags with zero stale ~/.epistemic primary paths.
